themes_detail.label: Tree Health Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints spiked to 26 THIS WEEK, a 407% jump from the 5.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.69), suggesting either environmental stress, pest outbreak, or storm damage concentrated in Tottenville/Great Kills—a district with longstanding forestry service budget requests that remain unfunded.
evidence: 26 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.1 weekly baseline (407% spike)
Z-score of 7.69 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Community Board has repeatedly requested forestry services and street tree maintenance funding (listed as recurring budget ask)
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about whether recent weather, pests, or infrastructure work triggered die-off
Investigate whether specific neighborhoods or tree species are affected disproportionately
Examine connection between unfunded forestry budget requests and inability to respond to crisis

themes_detail.label: Residential Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints jumped 125% THIS WEEK to 50 complaints from a 22.2 weekly average (z-score: 5.2), marking a sustained escalation in quality-of-life issues across the district with no clear localized cause yet identified.
evidence: 50 noise-residential complaints THIS WEEK vs. 22.2 weekly average (125% increase)
Z-score of 5.2 indicates highly statistically significant spike
Noise complaints represent 335 total complaints over 90 days, suggesting chronic baseline issue now worsening
reporting_angles: Canvas affected blocks to identify common sources (construction, bars, events, vehicle traffic)
Check whether specific addresses or venues are repeat offenders
Interview NYPD about enforcement capacity given district's longstanding request for new precinct facility

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Complaint Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints exploded 3100% THIS WEEK to 4 complaints from a 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 11.72, the highest severity spike in the dataset), suggesting a single event or new recurring use pattern requiring immediate localized investigation.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3100% spike)
Highest z-score in entire dataset (11.72) indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Previously near-zero baseline suggests this is a new phenomenon, not chronic issue
reporting_angles: Identify which specific parks are generating complaints (Great Kills Park, Conference House Park, etc.)
Determine if spike is event-driven (concert, rally, festival) or reflects new recurring use (youth gathering, gaming tournaments)
Interview Parks Department and NYPD about park monitoring and noise enforcement

themes_detail.label: Infrastructure Decay: Signs and Structural Issues
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints jumped 433% LAST WEEK to 6 complaints from 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.63), while flooring/stairs complaints spiked 264% THIS WEEK to 5 complaints, suggesting broader deterioration of public and possibly residential infrastructure requiring coordinated response.
evidence: 6 missing street sign complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (433% spike, z-score: 4.63)
5 flooring/stairs complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 baseline (264% spike, z-score: 3.65)
Street condition complaints already high at 1,778 over 90 days; Community Board repeatedly requests street reconstruction funding
reporting_angles: Map which streets are missing signs to identify geographic pattern or system-wide issue
Determine if flooring/stairs complaints are concentrated in buildings with aging infrastructure or specific landlords
Connect to DOT's repeated budget requests for street reconstruction—assess whether deferred maintenance is manifesting in complaints

themes_detail.label: Off-Leash Dog Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints spiked 500% LAST WEEK to 3 complaints from a 0.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.54), a small absolute number but statistically significant, potentially indicating new park use patterns or enforcement gaps in a district requesting stronger NYPD presence.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score: 3.54)
Spike coincides with park noise explosion, suggesting possible shared root cause (increased park usage)
District has longstanding request for new NYPD facility, raising questions about enforcement capacity
reporting_angles: Determine if spike is tied to same parks where noise complaints increased
Canvass dog owners and park-goers about whether enforcement or park usage patterns have shifted
Brief mention in broader park management story rather than standalone
